newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary Postabank needs structure changes - watchdog.
newsitem.headline: Hungary Postabank needs structure changes - watchdog.

text.p: Resolving structural problems will take time for Hungary's second largest bank, Postabank and needs the management's determination, the state banking wathchdog APTF said on Friday.

"Capital increases only will not resolve the problems, although they are indispensable parts of the solution," APTF Deputy Chairman Rezso Nyers told a news conference following a meeting of Postabank at which shareholders approved a capital hike.
Postabank was hit by rumour-induced withdrawal of deposits worth about 24 billion forints ($126 million) in February.

The shareholders approved on Friday a 7.1 billion forint capital hike by mainly domestic investors to 23.6 billion and the bank plans a second increase of about 10 billion forints later this year by a foreign investor, as yet unchosen.

Answering journalists' questions, Nyers revealed that APTF had written to all of the bank's directors calling for changes in its organisation and business policies. "The bank must be made more organised and transparent and these factors must match the bank's increased size," he said.

According to the consolidated balance sheet approved on Friday, Postabank group boosted its balance sheet total to 402.3 billion forints from 281.9 billion in 1996, with most of the increase coming from the bank's expansion.
However, profits fell to 184 million forints from 2.41 billion in 1995 despite a 12 billion government guarantee on its assets, granted following the withdrawals.
Nyers said Postabank must stop expansion, concentrate on stabilisation and replace the accumulated loss-making assets with profitable ones even if this causes imminent losses.

"This is a very difficult task which needs time and has only begun, and perhaps the management should embrace the idea a little better," Nyers said. "Replacing the assets slowly, will be a hard slog."
The government has recently approved swap of assets worth 17 billion forints between Postabank and the state privatisation agency APV.

Postabank CEO and Chairman Gabor Princz told shareholders that the bank would restructure its investments portfolio and was likely to set up a separate investment banking unit this year, perhaps based on its brokerage arm Postabank Securities.
With Friday's capital increase, the state boosted its indirect influence in the bank over 50 percent.
APTF said that the capital hike breached the credit institution law as the social security health care fund boosted its stake over a 15 percent limit to about 17 percent.
The capital hike did not jeopardise the bank's operations but APTF called on Postabank to achieve the reduction of the health care funds' stake, the watchdog said.
